biggest_catch: These are bill credits, not cash — they lower your Duke Energy bill. The headline $150 + $50/year is the smart-thermostat option; other options pay less, and you're letting Duke adjust your appliances during peak demand a few times a month.
catches: Payouts are bill credits, not cash — they reduce your Duke Energy bill.
The $150-off-next-bill + $50/year headline is the Smart Thermostat Option only; AC option pays $50 + $8 off May–November bills; heat strips $50 + $8 Dec–April; water heater $25 + $5 Dec–April.
You agree to let Duke adjust your enrolled appliances during peak demand, a few times per month.
Duke installs any needed equipment for free — but participation means ceding some control of your thermostat/AC.
The verified terms are from the income-qualified program page; confirm your region's general Power Manager page for the same amounts.

steps: Confirm you're a Duke Energy residential customer.
Pick your enrollment option: smart thermostat ($150 + $50/year), air conditioning ($50 + $8 summer bills), heat strips, or water heater.
Enroll in Power Manager — Duke installs any necessary equipment for free (call 866-541-8886 if you want help).
Allow Duke to adjust your enrolled appliance a few times per month during peak demand.
Watch the credits land: $150 off your next bill (thermostat option), plus annual credits while you stay enrolled.
timing: Enrollment credit off your next bill; annual credits post while enrolled.
